key_idea: Turn each valid school (all letters distinct and among the first p) into a 26-bit mask; the answer is the largest set of pairwise disjoint masks, found by trying all subsets of at most 20 teams.
sketch: Discard teams whose initials repeat a letter or use a letter beyond the p-th problem. Encode the rest as bitmasks and run an include/exclude DFS carrying the OR of chosen masks, with a trivial bound prune (count + remaining <= best). At most 2^20 states, O(2^t). Pitfalls: repeated letters make a team impossible, identical initials on two teams conflict with each other, and initials can be up to 80 characters long.
